findings.description: The new `fullShaLink` pattern begins each attempt at every `](` and scans `[^)\s]*` to the end of the line before backtracking to find `/commit/`, so a long line with many `](` and no `)` costs about O(n²). The replaced literal-base regex was linear in the line length for the same input, and the audit runs this scan on every entry line of the notes file.
findings.title: Commit-link scan can backtrack quadratically on long lines

citations.citation: // base equals the repository URL as text (T-037: no expression is built from input). A URL

evidence.explanation: A line of `](` repeated without a `)` gives each start position a forward scan to end of line plus a backtrack over the same characters, so total work grows with the square of the line length. The same shape already exists in `anyCommitLink`, so this PR adds a second instance of it rather than introducing a new class of risk; the impact is limited to unusually long hand-edited lines.

findings.description: In `ownShas`, the fixed pattern `(?<!\)\]\(([^)\s]*)\/commit\/...` lets the base run across an earlier unescaped `](`, so `matchAll` consumes the entry's own link inside the first match and never reports it. For a hand-edited line such as `](https://evil/a](https://github.com/o/r/commit/<sha>)`, the old literal-base regex found the own SHA and the new one reports `entry not linked`. The markdown-links verdict still fails in both versions because the line text differs from the expected line, so only the detail text changes; the ticket's and the code comment's claim that the same links are captured does not hold for these lines.
findings.title: Hand-edited link lines get a new detail text, same verdict

evidence.explanation: The base class `[^)\s]*` admits `]` and `(`, so one match can span a stray `](`; the old base was a literal URL that could not. The review-2 comment already notes that malformed lines differ in detail text, but the journal still says the report is byte-identical, and the code comment's 'captures the whole base' reasoning is only true for renderer-written lines.
